Hi John / Emily,

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation and helpful signal on where Acme wants the assistant to help (support triage, contract summarization, and internal SOP lookup). Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

- Recommended models to evaluate initially: rw-13b-quant (cost-optimized), rw-70b-fp16 (high-accuracy fallback). We've run internal benchmarks on similar enterprise support workloads — link below.
- To do model-fit/eval properly we need a representative prompt set and the edge cases you care about (PII-heavy transcripts, truncated inputs, instructions with multi-step constraints).
- Please upload a sample of your prompts + any redaction guidance to the shared Drive link by EOD 2026-06-18 so our Eval team can run quality/regression checks and produce a short comparative report.

I've attached a simple CSV template to get you started (acme_prompt_set_v1.csv) and a brief doc with recommended redaction patterns (redaction_guidance.docx). If you prefer S3, let me know and we can share upload credentials.

Deliverables we'll produce after you upload:
- Prompt-level evaluation across the two recommended model profiles (latency, token cost, correctness metrics)
- A short list of prompt/format tweaks and an example of a redaction-aware prompt pipeline
- Quality regression guardrails and a suggested canary rollout plan (canary size suggestions based on your expected traffic)

Next step: please confirm who on your side will own the prompt upload (and whether they need S3 or Drive access). I'll schedule a 30m sync for the week of 6/22 to review results.

Thanks,

Adding a couple of technical notes that are useful for Acme as they collect prompts: 

- When you export examples, please include: prompt text, expected/desired response (if available), and a label for "sensitive" when the prompt contains PII or contractual identifiers. That lets us run redaction-aware evals.
- Edge cases to call out explicitly: extremely long contexts (>> 2k tokens), nested instructions ("summarize then extract clauses"), hallucination-prone queries (open-ended fact requests), and multilingual snippets.
- For benchmarking, we'll run: accuracy/ROUGE-style match where we have ground truth, syntactic extraction accuracy for contract clauses, and a small suite of adversarial prompts to probe hallucination.
- Regression concern: please flag any recent prompt changes you rolled out in the last 30 days — those are the ones most likely to show distribution shift.

Suggested baseline stack for your eval run:
- Baseline: rw-13b-quant (good cost/latency tradeoff)
- Fallback/High-quality: rw-70b-fp16
- Safety/regression check: run a lightweight safety classifier on outputs and log any PII leakage cases for manual review.

I'll prepare a short eval rubric to attach to the Drive folder later today.

-rishi
Senior ML Engineer, Redwood Inference

Marissa / Rishi,

Thanks — this is helpful. Emily and I will pull together a first batch of 200 prompts and edge-case examples. A couple of quick clarifications: 

1) For the "expected response" column — is it OK if some rows use bullets for the expected answer vs free-text? We have a mix across teams.
2) For redaction, should we replace PII with tokens like [NAME], [SSN] or remove the fields entirely? We have legal preferences but can adapt if you recommend one approach.
3) We'll likely use our internal S3 bucket for upload. Can you confirm what ACLs/credentials format you need?

We should be able to upload by Friday 6/18. If anything slips, we'll let you know earlier.

Subject: Re: Prompt set collection & model-fit follow-up - Acme Corp

Perfect — thanks John. Quick answers inline and next steps: 

1) Expected response format: bullets are fine. In the CSV, please put the canonical expected response in the "expected_response" column as plain text; we will parse bullets as separate lines but keeping them in one cell is easiest for bulk eval.

2) Redaction: prefer token placeholders (e.g., [NAME], [EMAIL], [ACCOUNT_ID]) rather than removing fields. That preserves prompt structure and helps us measure leakage. The attached redaction_guidance.docx includes recommended tokens and regexes your legal team can review.

3) S3 upload: that's fine. We'll send a short IAM role + temporary credentials workflow. For now you can upload to the Drive folder if that's faster; we can move to S3 once we share the upload role.

Action items for Acme (please do by 2026-06-18):
- Upload CSV of ~200 prompts to the Drive link or to S3 (confirm which)
- Mark sensitive rows with a "sensitive" boolean and provide an "expected_response" where possible
- Add a short doc listing any recent changes to prompts/UX in the last 30 days

We'll run the eval and share a short report + model recommendations the week of 6/22. We'll also include a small checklist for canary rollout that covers monitoring thresholds (latency, error rate, quality regression).

If you want, I can set a 15-min checkpoint on 6/17 to see progress — say 11:00am PT?

Thanks again — looking forward to the prompts.

Marissa
